script.speaker: brooke
script.text: small table tonight, dinner crew: just the four of us by the water. where are we eating?

script.speaker: cyrus
script.text: I have a proposal. On Sunday I bought a bamboo mat, a bag of short-grain rice and a stack of seaweed sheets, and tried to roll my own.

script.speaker: cyrus
script.text: Eleven attempts. Every one unrolled itself on the way to the plate. I would now like to eat some made by a professional.

script.speaker: maya
script.text: cyrus. you followed the instructions and LOST? i need photos immediately

script.speaker: mina
script.text: i was there for attempt seven :) it tasted lovely, it just came apart in the soy dish. i think he was very brave

script.speaker: cyrus
script.text: Mina, I've already ruled places out for you. Same standard as sushi day: a whole part of the menu with no fish and no meat in it, so you can point at anything.

script.speaker: mina
script.text: you planned for me before i'd even opened a menu :) a whole page of rolls i can actually have, like that day... that would make my week

script.speaker: brooke
script.text: the legendary sushi day. i've heard about it so often i'm counting it as my own memory

script.speaker: cyrus
script.text: One more lesson from Sunday. The kit came with a little sesame dressing. I read the label anyway: peanut, third ingredient. It was in the bin before the rice finished cooking.

script.speaker: brooke
script.text: good. the satay incident stays a one-off. that story doesn't get a sequel, whatever sauce it comes in

script.speaker: maya
script.text: my turn. the trip fund finished its job, so i'm officially a two-dollar-sign person now

script.speaker: maya
script.text: three signs won't sink me anymore. but i will bring it up at every dinner from now until i'm on that coast

script.speaker: brooke
script.text: months of hearing about one bill. honestly, tempting

script.speaker: mina
script.text: maya, i missed the big news the other night and i want to hear all of it properly. could we find somewhere calm and hushed, where nobody has to shout across the table?

script.speaker: brooke
script.text: you all know i'm usually the one dragging us into the loud, packed spots. but yes. a calm room tonight, no crowd noise. let's actually talk

script.speaker: brooke
script.text: and in return, my one ask for the food: simple and light. nothing that's been battered and dunked in hot oil

script.speaker: cyrus
script.text: Noted, all of it. Assistant, I've done enough rolling for one week. Your turn.
